Show one 3D scene from several views

Source: R/facet-views.R
facet_views.Rd

facet_views() draws all data of a coord_3d() plot once per view, one panel per camera, like the multi-view drawings of engineering graphics and the shared views of matplotlib's 3D axes. Every panel shows the same scene with the same x, y and z scales and the same magnification, so a length measures the same on the page in every orthographic view.

Usage

facet_views(
  views = c("front", "top", "right", "isometric"),
  layout = c("wrap", "third_angle", "first_angle"),
  nrow = NULL,
  ncol = NULL,
  labeller = "label_value",
  strip.position = "top",
  lights = NULL,
  combine = c("cross", "pair")
)

Arguments

views

Views to draw, in panel order: a character vector of camera_3d() preset names, or a named list whose entries are preset names or lists of camera arguments such as camera_3d("front") or list(azimuth = 30, elevation = 20). Camera arguments a view leaves out come from coord_3d(). Names label the panels; unnamed preset entries are labelled by the preset name. NULL uses the coordinate's camera.

layout

Panel placement: "wrap" fills a grid row by row, "third_angle" and "first_angle" place the principal views by the projection method.

nrow, ncol

Grid dimensions of the "wrap" layout.

labeller, strip.position

Panel strip labeller and position, as in ggplot2::facet_wrap(). Use theme(strip.text = element_blank()) for a drawing without view names.

lights

NULL inherits coordinate lighting. A named list of lights from lights_3d(), light_3d() or the individual light constructors supplies lighting conditions; a NULL list entry selects an unlit panel.

combine

"cross" visits the lights in order for each camera; "pair" pairs the specifications, broadcasting a singleton. Shared guides use the first panel's camera and lighting as their reference. Engineering layouts accept one lighting condition.

Value

A ggplot2 Facet.

Details

With layout = "third_angle" or "first_angle" the panels follow the projection methods of ISO 5456-2. The views are recognised by name: "front", "top", "bottom", "left", "right" and "rear". In third-angle projection the top view sits above the front view and the right view to its right; in first-angle projection the top view sits below the front view and the right view to its left. The rear view sits at the end of the row. Further views, such as an isometric one, fill the free corners, first the upper right. Views in one row share their vertical page positions and views in one column their horizontal ones, so an edge seen in two adjacent views lines up across them.

The layers and their statistics are computed once; the panels differ only in their camera and lighting. The plot's layer data therefore all belong to the first panel.

See also

camera_3d() for the named views, view_3d() with link to turn several views together in the browser.

Examples

block <- expand.grid(x = 1:4, y = 1:3, z = 1:3)
block <- block[block$z == 1 | (block$x == 1 & block$y < 3), ]
p <- ggplot2::ggplot(block, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_voxel_3d(fill = "grey80", colour = "grey20") +
  coord_3d()
p + facet_views()
p + facet_views(c("front", "top", "right", iso = "isometric"), layout = "third_angle")
p + facet_views(c("front", "top", "right", iso = "isometric"), layout = "first_angle")
p + facet_views(list(a = list(azimuth = -30), b = list(azimuth = 60, zoom = 0.8)))
p + facet_views(views = NULL, lights = list(
  left = lights_3d(light_directional(c(-1, 1, 2))),
  right = lights_3d(light_directional(c(1, 1, 2)))))
